name: Cultural conservatism
summary: Cultural conservatism seeks to protect the cultural heritage of a nation or wider culture: its traditions, language, customs and shared values. It favors assimilation of newcomers into the dominant culture, is critical of multiculturalism, and is often linked to immigration restriction and defense of traditional family and religion. It is a disposition about identity and continuity more than an economic program, so adherents differ on markets and welfare.
scope: The contemporary cultural-conservative family as described by Wikipedia (assimilationist, monocultural, protective of national heritage, as in Leitkultur arguments and Quebec language protection), grounded in the Burke/Kirk/Scruton conservative tradition summarized by SEP. Excludes the narrower moral agenda of social conservatism and ethnic or racial nationalism.

keyFigures.name: Edmund Burke
keyFigures.role: Founding thinker of modern conservatism, defender of inherited institutions and custom

keyFigures.name: Russell Kirk
keyFigures.role: American traditionalist who set out conservative principles of custom and moral order

keyFigures.name: Roger Scruton
keyFigures.role: British philosopher who defended national culture, tradition and market limits within custom

sources.title: Conservatism (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Conservative themes of tradition, organic society, gradual change, authority and community; Scruton, Oakeshott and Kirk on markets, obedience and religion

sources.title: Cultural conservatism (Wikipedia)
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition as protection of national or cultural heritage; assimilation, criticism of multiculturalism, immigration, distinction from social conservatism

sources.title: Reflections on the Revolution in France (Burke, Gutenberg edition)
sources.author: Edmund Burke
sources.usedFor: Burkean case for change that preserves, inherited constitutional order and against revolution

sources.title: Ten Conservative Principles
sources.author: Russell Kirk (Kirk Center)
sources.usedFor: Moral order, custom, prescription, prudence, property, local community, limits on power

universal-healthcare.rationale: Cultural conservatism is about heritage and identity, not health financing; adherents split between welfare-state and market positions, and SEP notes conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The ideology is indifferent on wage floors; paternalist adherents may favor them and market-minded ones oppose, so no stated position exists.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: SEP records Scruton defending markets only within custom and moral tradition and warning against free-market doctrine, so adherents are split.

public-ownership.rationale: Kirk's defense of private property and local community cuts against state ownership of industry, though the ideology never addresses it directly.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax levels are not a cultural question; adherents range from fiscal conservatives to paternalists.

unions-good.rationale: Kirk values voluntary associations, but unions as such are not a cultural-conservative concern, and adherents differ on them.

property-fundamental.rationale: Kirk's seventh principle ties private property to freedom, independence and culture, though he adds that owners bear duties.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Scruton-style conservatives criticize market excess on cultural grounds while others defend business, so adherents are genuinely split.

cut-welfare.rationale: No cultural-conservative position; some stress family and community over the state, others accept paternalist welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's preference for inherited property arrangements and wariness of radical economic reorganization; not directly addressed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Conservatives value order, but Burke-style distrust of concentrated power pulls the other way; not a defining issue.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the concern for moral order and social norms; cultural conservatives generally resist drug liberalization, though it is not a defining issue.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not a central concern; adherents often object to speech codes as imposed progressive norms, though some favor protecting national sentiment.

strong-leader.rationale: Kirk's ninth principle calls for limits and balance on power, and Burke favored inherited constitutional restraints over a leader bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: Conservatives treat the state and inherited institutions as essential to order; Burke and Scruton reject anarchism outright.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the rural, traditionalist culture many adherents defend; the ideology does not address gun law directly.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's emphasis on order and the 'tolerably ordered' society; not stated for police funding specifically.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Cultural conservatives uphold traditional moral norms and generally oppose commercial sex, as a matter of the moral order Kirk describes.

decide-locally.rationale: Kirk's eighth principle says matters are best settled by families and local bodies rather than distant central authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Conservatives stress imperfect human nature and order, but the rehabilitation versus punishment balance is not stated and adherents differ.

traditional-family.rationale: Kirk values custom and community and cultural conservatives defend inherited ways of life, but the Wikipedia article distinguishes cultural conservatism from the social conservatism that carries the family agenda.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Adherents generally oppose redefining marriage as departing from tradition, though the ideology is more culture than morals focused and some accept it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Abortion is an issue of social conservatism that Wikipedia distinguishes from cultural conservatism; most adherents lean against it but it is not central.

more-religion-public.rationale: Kirk and Burke treat religion as part of the inherited order, but SEP notes some conservatives like Oakeshott were secular, so only a moderate yes.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Burke-style gradualism and distrust of rationalist social engineering make adherents wary of active programs to redress history.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Kirk's enduring moral order and inherited customs imply that gender distinctions are not merely constructed, though this is inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Wikipedia defines cultural conservatism as seeking to protect the cultural heritage of a nation or culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Burke's line that a state without means of change lacks means of conservation, and Kirk's tenth principle, both call for reform that respects institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Wikipedia links the ideology to opposition to immigration, though cultural conservatives vary between cutting numbers and demanding assimilation.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Conservative stress on local, inherited loyalties makes adherents wary of supranational bodies, though this is inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Not a cultural issue; adherents split between market-friendly and protectionist, community-protecting positions.

nation-first.rationale: Defending national heritage implies priority for the national community, though Wikipedia notes cultural conservatism differs from nationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The ideology does not address it; Burke-style caution against abstract rights crusades competes with moral-order arguments.

open-borders.rationale: Open borders would end the control over culture that cultural conservatives seek; Wikipedia ties the ideology to immigration restriction and assimilation.

limit-growth.rationale: Not addressed; some adherents like Scruton care for environmental stewardship, others defend growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Scruton wrote on conservation as love of home while other adherents resist state-led action; no settled position.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Kirk's imperfectability principle and the conservative anti-utopianism SEP describes reject faith that progress solves most problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is not a cultural question and the tradition took no position, so adherents differ by temperament and country.

revolution-justified.rationale: Burke's Reflections is a founding case against revolutionary rupture, and Kirk holds radicals who discard custom make things worse.

experts-over-public.rationale: Conservatives distrust abstract rationalism but also prize authority; adherents often resent expert elites on cultural issues.

central-planning.rationale: SEP reports conservative opposition to rationalist planning of society, as in Burke and Oakeshott.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's commitment to private property; the issue is not addressed directly.

land-value-tax.rationale: No cultural-conservative position on tax design.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's view that property and continuity across generations support a free society.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between family-and-work traditionalists and paternalists.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Adherents split between those protecting communities from economic disruption and free-market conservatives.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Conservative wariness of planning suggests no, but the ideology takes no stand and some adherents favor industrial policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Kirk ties widespread property to independence and culture, but he does not specifically urge distribution among small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Kirk and Burke defend property and the inherited economic order; abolishing money is never discussed but runs against that.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not a cultural issue; inferred from conservative institutional caution.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Kirk favors intermediate associations, but state-recognized wage setting is not part of the cultural program.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kirk's ninth principle demands restraints on power, so single-party rule fits poorly, though some authoritarian adherents differ.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Burke defended hereditary monarchy as part of an inherited constitution, and cultural conservatives generally value such continuity.

democracy-best.rationale: Conservatives accept democratic forms but distrust majority rule in the abstract; adherents split.

direct-votes.rationale: Burke defended representation by judgment rather than direct popular mandate, and conservatives distrust plebiscitary rationalism.

workers-councils.rationale: Replacing parliaments with councils is the kind of radical constitutional break Burke opposed; the sources do not discuss councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from attachment to an established national culture; Quebec-style cultural conservatism complicates it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Kirk accepts differences in condition and orders, and Burke favored a natural aristocracy, though this is not about cultural conservatism as such.

political-violence-never.rationale: Burke condemned revolutionary violence yet accepted force in defense of order; the statement is too absolute to answer cleanly.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between martial-virtue and prudential views.

separate-church-state.rationale: Kirk's transcendent order and Burke's religious establishment favor links between religion and the state, though cultural conservatives vary.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Burke and Kirk see religion informing law, but SEP says religion is not essential and adherents do not demand scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Conservatives treat courts, defense and policing as core inherited state functions; privatizing them is a libertarian position.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from national pride and preserving the nation, but not stated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wikipedia describes cultural, not ethnic, definitions of the nation, with assimilation open to newcomers; some adherents lean ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Conservatives reject class conflict as history's engine; Kirk defends orders and continuity.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Kirk's variety principle rejects forced leveling beyond equality before God and law.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents value heritage but also property law and national unity.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from distrust of historical redress and Burkean gradualism.

civilizational-union.rationale: Civilizational thinkers like Huntington are discussed, but union across states is not a cultural-conservative aim.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Kirk and Burke stress duty and moral order over self-interest as a good in itself.

duties-before-rights.rationale: SEP records conservative stress on duty and obedience, and Kirk's moral order, over abstract rights, but adherents do not abandon rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between stewardship and indifference.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from pro-family emphasis and anxieties about demographic decline.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Some conservatives lament modernity, but Kirk defends property and an inherited civilization, so a disaster verdict is not the mainstream.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Deliberately speeding disruptive change contradicts Burke's gradualism and Kirk's prudence.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's enduring human nature and imperfectability; not addressed directly.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from conservative distrust of rationalist technocratic government.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The tradition predates the question and nothing in its principles settles it; order-minded and liberty-minded adherents differ.

restore-past-order.rationale: Burke wanted reform and preservation, not restoration of a lost order, but cultural decline narratives pull the other way; adherents are split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Oakeshott described conservatism as a disposition rather than a creed and favored practical judgment over doctrine.

direct-action.rationale: Kirk and Burke favor working through established institutions, though street activism on cultural issues is accepted by some.

means-match-ends.rationale: Oakeshott treats politics as practical judgment, but the tradition makes no claim that methods must mirror the desired society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The sources defend inherited civilisation and culture; abandoning civilisation is not discussed but runs against them.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kirk defends the orders and distinctions of an inherited society; the division of labour itself is not discussed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Kirk rejects economic levelling and ties property to freedom; distribution by need is not discussed directly.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from commitment to private property; not directly addressed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Conservatism rejects Marxian exploitation theory and defends property and profit with duties.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Burke condemned revolutionary overthrow of inherited order; class dictatorship is not discussed directly.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivizing land contradicts Kirk's property principle and local community.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a cultural-conservative claim; adherents reject Marxist historical determinism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Conservatives accept the state's legitimate functions, though libertarian-leaning adherents disagree.

harm-principle.rationale: Cultural conservatives accept restricting conduct to protect shared moral and cultural norms, not only to prevent harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Kirk's community and variety principles stress groups, families and associations as bearers of rights and duties.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between patriotic duty and individual liberty.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred from the conservative commitment to rooted attachment to home and nation.

state-as-business.rationale: Conservatives see the state as a moral and historical community, not a firm with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; paternalist adherents may agree and libertarian ones not.

media-academia-power.rationale: Cultural conservatives commonly claim that universities and media shape culture against tradition, though the claim is a modern complaint and not a founding doctrine.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Wikipedia notes critics accuse the ideology of racism but defines it by culture, not biology; adherents mostly emphasize culture.

organic-representation.rationale: Burke's organic society and Kirk's emphasis on families and local bodies suggest this, though modern cultural conservatives rarely propose it.

total-state.rationale: Totalizing state control is contrary to Kirk's limits on power and voluntary community.

national-rebirth.rationale: Cultural conservatives mourn decline but pursue preservation and gradual repair, not radical rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Protecting existing national culture does not imply expansion; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Medieval personal fealty is not a modern cultural-conservative demand.

bound-labor.rationale: Kirk ties property to freedom; serfdom is not discussed in the sources, so the answer follows from that principle.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Conservatives hold to an enduring moral order and distrust relativism, though SEP notes the debate on relativism within conservatism.

universal-morality.rationale: Kirk's first principle asserts a transcendent moral order, though Oakeshott-style adherents are more particularist.

single-common-good.rationale: Oakeshott and Burke reject rationalist blueprints of a single common good worked out by reason.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The ideology is a general disposition about protecting national cultures, with no settled view on this specific national claim.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Protecting a nation's culture could support or oppose citizenship for diaspora members, and the sources do not decide it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Wikipedia mentions Quebec language protection as a cultural-conservative cause, and language is a cultural heritage.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from conservative authority and property positions.

school-vouchers.rationale: Adherents split between support for parental choice and support for common national schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is separate from culture, and SEP shows conservatives disagreeing over economic doctrine.

economic-freedom.rationale: SEP shows conservatives split on free-market doctrine, with Scruton critical of its drift.

rule-by-example.rationale: Kirk and Burke value moral example and civic virtue but also law and constitutional checks.

national-self-determination.rationale: Preserving a nation's culture implies the right of nations to govern themselves.

force-without-un.rationale: Cultural conservatism says little about foreign intervention, and adherents divide between nationalist assertiveness and Burkean caution.

reason-over-faith.rationale: SEP reports the conservative skepticism of reason and the value of prejudice and tradition, central to Burke and Kirk.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Reserving benefits for members of the national community follows from restricting immigration and defending a shared culture.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed by the cultural program; adherents split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Kirk and Burke treat society as an organic whole of mutual obligations rather than class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The Wikipedia article defines the ideology as protecting a nation's cultural heritage; the statement's trade-off is not discussed but runs directly against it.

dominated-front.rationale: A common front of countries against Western powers is an anti-imperial idea outside the cultural-conservative program.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from national loyalty over international class identity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Cultural conservatives defend traditional gender roles in society, but law fixing them is not a defined position.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from acceptance of commerce within custom.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Wikipedia defines the ideology by culture and assimilation, not racial classification; mainstream adherents reject this.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Conservatives reject the Marxist view of the state as class tool and treat it as a historical, moral community.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not a cultural matter and adherents differ, from rural producers to Scruton-style stewardship supporters.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Wikipedia says proponents favor assimilation into the dominant culture and view monoculturalism as supporting unity.

elite-replacement.rationale: Wikipedia notes critics, and conspiracy claims like replacement are a fringe, not typical adherent, view.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral design is not addressed, and Burke-style conservatives lean to the inherited system in each country.

national-mission.rationale: Burke-style caution about exporting systems makes adherents lean against, though inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Cultural conservatives defend traditional social arrangements and would not describe them as systemic male advantage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Cultural conservatives often portray elites as out of touch with ordinary culture, but it is not a doctrinal claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic state coercion conflicts with Kirk's moral order and family emphasis.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Conservatives value order and the security forces but also the rule of law, and the sources give no view on accountability for past abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Cultural conservatives generally accept a larger role for the state in culture, but adherents vary on economy.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Wikipedia defines the ideology as cultural, and most adherents reject race-based discouragement, though some fringe groups hold it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kirk affirms equality before God and the law while rejecting equality of condition.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Inferred from defense of established national heritage.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Assimilationist cultural conservatives favor one common law and culture over parallel legal systems, as in the German Leitkultur argument.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The ideology takes no view on legal limits on conversion, and adherents split between religious-freedom and tradition-protecting positions.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not a general cultural-conservative position; specific to Hindu nationalism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Kirk's transcendent order implies religion has a place in education, though secular adherents differ.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Kirk wants power limited and balanced, which cuts against a permanently strengthened state, though the issue is a Marxist-Leninist one the tradition never addressed.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Burke grounded legitimacy in prescription and inherited constitution rather than consent, though modern adherents accept elections.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade goals are not part of the cultural program, and adherents are split on trade policy.

population-transfer.rationale: Wikipedia says assimilation, not removal, is the stated goal, and the practice is not part of the mainstream doctrine.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Conservatives accept state coercion for order, so the absolute principle fits poorly.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Conservatives doubt progress as a driving idea and also doubt perfectibility, but the tradition never states this claim, so it stays neutral.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's concern for order and limited toleration of subversion.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept of non-domination is not part of the conservative vocabulary, and the tradition takes no stated position.

separated-powers.rationale: Kirk's principles call for prudent restraints on power; the sources speak of conservatism in general, not of cultural conservatism's constitutional views.

vanguard-party.rationale: Burke condemned revolutionary rupture; a vanguard party is not discussed but is that kind of project.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Paternalist conservatives favor obligations to the poor while market-leaning adherents resist priority rules, so the ideology is split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Property ownership is favored by Kirk but this is a policy matter without cultural content.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor law is outside the cultural program, and conservatives disagree on balancing union and employer power.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred; conservatives usually point to institutions and culture instead.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Wikipedia attributes to proponents the claim that homogeneous communities have more trust, although it is contested.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Burke's reliance on inherited institutions runs against new rationalist devices like sortition; the sources do not discuss lotteries.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kirk wants order but also restraints on power; adherents split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred from commitment to property and markets within custom.

party-controls-media.rationale: Control of the media by a party violates the limits on power and voluntary community in Kirk's principles.

party-commands-army.rationale: Kirk's demand for limits on power makes party command of the army an unattractive arrangement, though the question is not addressed directly.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Cultural conservatives favor demanding integration before membership, as in citizenship test debates described by Wikipedia.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Burke saw representation as a role of deliberate judgment, not wage parity.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Internal party rules are not part of the cultural-conservative program, and the tradition is itself skeptical of ideological parties.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The ideology protects national heritage and Wikipedia cites One Nation and others that resist supranational erosion, though not all adherents are Eurosceptic.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Depends on the adherent's own church, so no shared position.

clerical-rule.rationale: Burke and Kirk favor religion informing society but not clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Cultural conservatives support national identity and loyalty; revolutionary defeatism is not discussed in the sources.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Kirk's moral order suggests sympathy, but adherents vary on censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Kirk wants restraints on power, which term limits support.

recall-officials.rationale: Burke rejected binding instructions from constituents.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses alliances; adherents who stress national sovereignty might support withdrawal, but security-minded ones keep alliances, so the lean is slight.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Kirk defends property and freedom, which rules out banning rental.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replacing a professional army with a citizen militia is not a conservative demand, and Kirk's emphasis on order and prudence points mildly against it.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Many cultural conservatives idealize rural community life, but it is not a core claim.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Protecting a national culture might favor reunification, but the sources show no doctrine on it and cases differ.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Common complaint among cultural conservatives about elite culture, but not doctrinal.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural conservatism holds that the dominant culture should be preserved and that some imported practices conflict with it.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from stress on order and moral desert; adherents split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Cultural and social conservatives generally resist progressive sex and gender curricula as undermining traditional norms.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious conservatives often support it, but secular adherents oppose it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Kirk's enduring moral order supports legal limits on pornography, but libertarian-leaning adherents differ.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Wikipedia stresses cultural assimilation, which pulls away from descent, while heritage emphasis pulls toward it.

minority-language-support.rationale: Assimilation priorities oppose support for minority languages, except Quebec-style protection of the dominant language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Adherents split between defending religious freedom and demanding common law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Kirk and Burke value custom and convention as sources of order, against Mill's celebration of eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from respect for property and contracts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Burke-style gradualism rejects transforming the property system as a condition of independence, but the tradition never addressed decolonization.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Burke opposed rewriting constitutions from scratch.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Kirk links freedom with property and prudence, so trading liberty for growth sits badly, though the sources do not address development dictatorship.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Conservatives prioritize obligations to home and community over distant strangers, but the ideology never rules on foreign aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national sovereignty and self-reliance; the sources do not discuss weapons policy.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not a cultural topic, and conservatives disagree on them.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from attachment to national heritage and homeland.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Kirk affirms property rights with attached duties, between the two readings.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: This is a dispute inside Marxism on how to classify the USSR, and cultural conservatives hold no distinctive view.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Burkean prudence supports caution, though not stated for environment.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the patriotic concern for national security and the usual conservative support for alliances such as NATO; not stated in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The ideology gives no rule for annexed territory, and adherents might emphasize either national claims or international law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Kirk and Burke treat religion as an independent pillar of inherited order; curbing church property is not discussed directly.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Burke's constitutional monarchy represents a head of state as a symbol of continuity above faction.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; Quebec-style cases complicate it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: One country two systems arrangements are not discussed by the tradition, and adherents split between unity and regional heritage.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Burke defended hereditary monarchy but not divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure has no cultural content, and conservatives are divided on it.

character-from-environment.rationale: SEP notes conservatives see human nature as fixed and imperfectible, so upbringing alone is not accepted.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Kirk requires limits on power and Burke defended constitutional law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space settlement is not a goal of heritage-protecting conservatism, and the progress-minded framing sits poorly with its skepticism of utopian projects.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Burke defended a mixed British constitution of crown, lords and commons.

leader-cult.rationale: Honoring leaders as embodiments of the nation conflicts with limits on power.

equal-parenting.rationale: Traditionalists favor mother-centered family roles, but adherents differ.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The statement belongs to Marxist-Leninist debates; cultural conservatives reject the class-struggle framework, so a mild disagree is the best inference.

land-redistribution.rationale: Kirk holds secure private property to be a basis of freedom; confiscating estates is not discussed directly.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not address refugee return, and adherents would weigh national culture against property and historical claims.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Wikipedia describes the ideology as protecting a culture within or beyond state borders, but claims on territory are not a doctrine.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Burke and Kirk value religion but modern adherents do not punish apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Wikipedia says cultural conservatives object to imported practices that clash with the dominant culture, but mainstream Western adherents do not seek to impose dress codes on women in law.

common-currency.rationale: National identity attachment makes adherents wary of replacing national currencies, though inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Cultural conservatism protects the heritage of existing nations, so cross-border political union of kin peoples is not a goal; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Defending a minority's own institutions fits culture-protection, but assimilationist adherents want one national culture, so they split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the assimilationist stress on integrating into the country of residence; the sources do not discuss diaspora strategy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Conservatives hold that ideas, customs and morals drive history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not a cultural issue, and market-defending and community-protecting conservatives disagree.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are an economic question without cultural content, with conservatives divided between market purists and defenders of established institutions.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Burke's constitutionalism values checks over unchecked majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas follow the progressive agenda that cultural conservatives resist.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A closed imperial bloc is not part of cultural conservatism; inferred from its focus on protecting culture, not autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade rules are outside the program, and conservatives disagree on supranational standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives by social duty is a collectivist program; Kirk's defense of property and its rewards suggests a mild no.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Burke opposed revolutionary violence; armed vanguard strategy is not discussed in the sources.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Burke defended inherited rank, Kirk defended variety of orders and conditions.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Protecting cultural heritage implies teaching the nation's own history at the centre.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial paternalism once had conservative defenders, but modern cultural conservatism says little on it and adherents split.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Wikipedia article ties cultural conservatism to a unified national identity; it does not discuss what schools should teach.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Conservatives resist group preferences on principle, though not a core cultural issue.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not addressed by the cultural program, so there is no stated position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Conservatives hold that institutions evolve through gradual adaptation, so a mild yes is inferred; the cultural program does not discuss capitalist crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Wikipedia notes Chinese promotion of traditional culture, but cultivating influence in former imperial regions is not a general doctrine.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory proposals fall outside the cultural-conservative program, with no stated position.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The labor-aristocracy thesis is a Marxist-Leninist theory, and cultural conservatives reject its class analysis, though they rarely address it.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Property rights versus community norms; adherents split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Burke prefers prescriptive rights over written declarations, but modern adherents accept them.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from respect for prescriptive standing.

elective-rulers.rationale: Burke favoured inheritance but modern adherents accept elections.

minority-veto.rationale: Burke favored deliberate institutions over unanimity rules.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Burke accepted the 1688 Revolution as defense of constitution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Burke defended the British parliamentary constitution.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Scruton wrote on animal welfare within duties, but not a core cultural issue.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Conservatives accept human use of animals within duties of stewardship and care; this is inferred and not a defining view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Kirk says property carries duties and varied orders imply obligations from those who hold standing.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Kirk and Burke emphasize civic duty and community participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Cultural conservatives criticize mass culture, but not as a tool reproducing the social order, which is a Frankfurt School claim.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is a Marxist analysis, and conservatives see social order as grounded in custom and legitimacy, not class manipulation.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not part of the tradition.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the priority given to national membership.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties and has no counterpart in cultural conservatism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is outside the program and the sources give no position.

return-lost-territory.rationale: National heritage might support claims to lost lands, but cultural conservatism is not irredentist by definition, so adherents split.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the stress on one assimilated national culture and the Burkean preference for existing constitutional arrangements.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Conservatives reject fascism but the statement bundles a constitutional doctrine on which the tradition is split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Kirk condemned totalitarian utopianism of all kinds, but he did not rest his principles on equating them, so the answer is inferred.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Contested claim; mainstream conservatives reject it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Protecting inherited cultural heritage is the defining aim, but the sources discuss heritage sites such as the Terracotta Army, not monuments to now-condemned figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist critique of gender policy.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The topic is not addressed by the sources, and traditionalists and men's-issues advocates among adherents disagree.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Wikipedia notes Huntington and Chinese advocates of traditional culture holding that civilisations are different.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Conservatives value order and the armed forces, but Kirk's limits on power argue against a political army, so adherents split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Traditionalists honor family care work but divide on paying for it with public money.

filial-duty.rationale: The only mention of Confucius in the Wikipedia article is in the example of China's state-led cultural revival, not a cultural-conservative doctrine of duties to parents; support is a guess from the general respect for tradition.

office-by-exam.rationale: Wikipedia mentions Confucian revival, but not stated for examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Protecting national heritage might favor blocking sales, while market-minded adherents oppose it, so adherents split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Defending traditional marriage means opposing easier divorce, though not defining.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Burke's famous view was that representatives owe judgment, not obedience to instructions, which is opposed to mandated delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not a cultural matter and conservatives are divided.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Kirk's defence of secure private property runs against tenure held only while land is used; the sources do not discuss land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitutional tradition of parliament holding the purse.

single-official-language.rationale: Wikipedia links the ideology to Quebec language protection and to Leitkultur in Germany.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Protecting national heritage might support limits on foreign land ownership, while property-minded adherents oppose, so adherents split.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Group-outcomes tests are a progressive position that cultural conservatives resist.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Scruton and other critics of market culture, but not defining.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Cultural conservatism offers no doctrine on covert warfare, and adherents divide between hawks and Burkean cautious realists.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The statement reflects Cold War bloc politics, with no counterpart in the cultural program.

corporate-influence.rationale: Cultural conservatives worry about corporate power over culture, but market defenders oppose limits on lobbying, so they split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Protecting national culture could support limits on foreign funding of NGOs, but the sources do not discuss it and adherents also value free association.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Preferring natural family growth over immigration follows from cultural continuity.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local control favors the restriction while property rights oppose it, so adherents split.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment policy has no cultural-conservative position and adherents are split.

democratic-peace.rationale: The thesis is not one the tradition discusses, and Burkean conservatives doubt exporting institutions.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: SEP records Scruton calling obedience the principal virtue of political subjects.

non-intervention.rationale: Conservatives hold no absolute rule on intervening abroad, and adherents split between prudential and nationalist approaches.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organization is not a cultural concern and the tradition has no stated view.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims are not part of the doctrine, but a fringe element.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Kirk's custom and continuity favour keeping inherited institutions such as legal marriage; the sources do not discuss the legal status of marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Conservatives value order and discretion in government, but accept openness norms, and the tradition takes no stated position.

local-production.rationale: Kirk favors local community, but not local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Informal affinity groups are an anarchist model, though Kirk values voluntary community, so the tradition has no stated view on movement structure.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Defending national heritage includes sovereignty of national law.

religious-nation.rationale: Wikipedia says cultural conservatism may be tied to religion, but not necessarily.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tributary international relations are a Sinocentric concept outside the cultural-conservative program, with no stated view.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional fiscal arrangements are not a cultural question, and Kirk's local community principle only partly applies.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Kirk defends private property, so personal belongings staying private is accepted, though the commons-for-production clause makes it only a mild yes.

defeat-communism.rationale: Kirk was anticommunist, but cultural conservatism is broader.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not a cultural matter, and conservatives are split between traditional public provision and market choice.

religion-illusion.rationale: Kirk and Burke treat religion as the source of moral order and community that endures, the opposite of an illusion that fades.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: SEP notes conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine, and many are ambivalent about capitalism eroding tradition.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Traditionalist and gradualist conservatives favor reform through custom and law, not economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Kirk stresses family, local community and voluntary association as the places of care, against state replacement.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language protection is a cultural-conservative concern (Quebec), but purging loanwords is not a stated position; adherents split.

treaties-binding.rationale: Respect for inherited agreements and prescription suggests honoring treaties; inferred from Burke and Kirk.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Kirk values local community but also private property, so common-property communes are rejected; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Assimilation is favored, but state-steered settlement conflicts with gradualism and limited government; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Conservatives reject communism, and views on capitalism vary; no consensus third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on protecting a nation's cultural heritage as a people's inheritance.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: the ideology is a mainstream disposition about heritage and does not involve denying historical atrocity.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: the sources separate cultural conservatism from the narrower moral agenda of social conservatism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Kirk's principles and the Burkean tradition call for limits on power and a lawful, prescriptive constitutional order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: it protects heritage, including religion as culture, but modern adherents rarely seek state penalties.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from its stress on organic, rooted community, which is at odds with ruling distant peoples for profit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: it would not hold a duty of Muslim resistance.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from Burke's case against revolution and for prescriptive, gradual change.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from Burke's view of representation and the tradition's preference for established authority over direct rule.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from its focus on shared national culture rather than group-based oppression analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from its defence of traditional norms and custom.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's moral order and its defence of traditional norms.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred from its roots in a tradition that defends inherited institutions over blending ideas.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the tradition values property and custom and does not use Marxist alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from its assimilationism and defence of the national culture, though adherents differ on how far.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Adherents differ: Kirk describes a transcendent moral order but Burke's tradition is not strictly theocratic.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: adherents differ between heritage-protecting secularism and defence of religious symbols.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no common view.

social-market-economy.rationale: SEP notes conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on national continuity and order.

rich-first.rationale: SEP notes conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; adherents differ on alliances.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from Burke's defence of inherited institutions, balanced against modern adherents who accept republics; adherents are split.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the Kirk principle that property and market order are preferable to leveling schemes; cooperative credit is not a conservative theme.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The ideology is about heritage, not economic policy, and adherents split on sovereignty versus orthodoxy.

property-franchise.rationale: Kirk and Burke value property, but modern cultural conservatives mostly accept universal suffrage; nothing in the sources endorses a wealth franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Never addressed; the tradition is critical of ideological projects that remake society along theoretical lines.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the Burkean and Kirkian defence of existing social order and markets against ideological critiques.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's view of property as bound with freedom; the tradition rejects the claim that private ownership hollows freedoms.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Kirk calls for prudent restraints upon power and Burke defends the inherited constitution and rule of law against arbitrary revolutionary power.

racial-franchise.rationale: The scope excludes ethnic or racial nationalism, and cultural conservatism is assimilationist rather than race-based.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition favors representative institutions but adherents differ on technology.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents are split between valuing publicity and valuing institutional discretion.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from its defence of traditional family and religion, though the sources describe no specific legal ban.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Cultural conservatism seeks assimilation, not shunning of groups, and the sources document no boycott of religious minorities.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Burke defends representation by elected, judging representatives rather than direct delegation, which cuts against citizens' assemblies by lot.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's emphasis on custom, prescription and a transcendent moral order over reinterpretation for modern conditions.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Conservatives such as Scruton accept markets within custom while many fear concentrated power, and the ideology is about heritage rather than economics, so adherents split; inferred from SEP.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the defense of traditional family and inherited custom; cultural conservatism is distinct from the narrower social-conservative agenda, so the answer is mild.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Cultural conservatives defend inherited religious heritage as part of national culture, so a state campaign against religion in schools is contrary to the core of the ideology.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Kirk's principles stress order, prudence and authority, and abolition would be a radical break with inherited institutions of the kind Burke defends.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred: the ideology favors a single shared national culture and assimilation over formal communal blocs, though pragmatic acceptance of power-sharing is possible.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from conservative emphasis on civil society, community and 'little platoons' over central government; adherents differ on welfare.

term-limits.rationale: Conservatives value continuity and experience in institutions but also distrust entrenched power; the ideology does not address the issue and adherents split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from Burke's view of representation by judgement and from distrust of novel institutional schemes; the issue is not addressed directly.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; concern for posterity fits Burke's partnership across generations but nothing makes this a top priority, so neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from deference to inherited religious tradition; cultural conservatism is a cultural disposition, not a doctrine on church office, so adherents differ.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Cultural conservatism defends the traditional family but is distinct from the stricter social-conservative agenda, and adherents split on spousal authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the assimilationist view that newcomers should join the national culture before shaping it; local voting rights for non-citizens are not discussed.

rent-control.rationale: The ideology is a cultural disposition and conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine, so adherents split on rent caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's respect for inherited institutions and property in Burke and Kirk; intellectual property is not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: the ideology defends heritage through custom and civil society, not drilled state youth organisations; it is not discussed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not part of cultural conservatism and adherents are not documented as taking a side.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The ideology is about cultural heritage rather than defence policy, and adherents split on alliances and bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; adherents differ on how national history should be officially judged.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Kirk's principles link property and freedom, so rewarding ownership is treated as legitimate; inferred, since the ideology is not an economic program.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the conservative tradition accepts the legitimacy of defensive force; the statement is not discussed in the sources.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Burke's partnership of the living, the dead and the unborn makes the nation a continuous inheritance, and Wikipedia describes the ideology as protecting heritage; Burke does not claim ancient ethnic origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the ideology's linkage to traditional family values; Wikipedia separates it from the narrower social-conservative agenda, and the sources do not address this.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its defence of traditional family and inherited categories; not discussed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The ideology honours inherited tradition but the sources do not address martyr veneration, and adherents differ by culture.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Burke and Kirk stress prudence and distrust of abstract crusades, which cuts against framing politics as a cosmic struggle; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology concerns protecting the national culture and not the structure of the diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: the ideology's aim is protecting cultural heritage and continuity, which it treats as prior to and sustaining the political order.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from its defence of traditional religion and family; adherents often keep inherited religious language, though the sources do not address it.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the defence of inherited religious tradition as a source of authority, not a thing to be judged by a modern standard; not discussed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The ideology concerns culture, not economic ownership, and adherents are not documented as taking a side.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not part of the ideology; no source discusses regional boundaries.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence is outside the ideology's concern with heritage; adherents differ.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from conservatism's wariness of class-based political programmes in favour of inherited institutions.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Ownership of local services is not a cultural question and adherents differ on it.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from the Burkean preference for balanced, inherited institutions that check popular majorities.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from conservative support for private property as a pillar of order, as in Kirk's principles.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Burke's 'little platoons' favour local attachments, but cultural conservatives defend the national culture; adherents differ.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the cultural conservative defence of the traditional family as a carrier of heritage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not addressed by the ideology.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is not addressed; adherents differ.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Payment privacy is not addressed by the ideology.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is not addressed; adherents split between privacy and order concerns.

person-over-state.rationale: Conservatives stress duties to community and tradition, while also defending individual dignity, so adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Kirk's Ten Conservative Principles begin with a belief in a transcendent order, and Burke defends religion as the basis of society.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Adherents split between defending local custom and a unified national culture; no stated position.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form is not addressed by the ideology.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Wikipedia distinguishes cultural conservatism from racial nationalism, since it defends a shared culture that newcomers can assimilate into rather than racial groups.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in national heritage is central, but pride in race as such is outside the scope, and adherents differ on ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed by the ideology; adherents differ on military use.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Wikipedia describes cultural conservatives as defining the nation by shared language and heritage and defending language protection such as Quebec's; common language and history as a basis of nationhood is a typical view.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the favor for assimilation into one national culture; separate electorates for communities would entrench parallel societies.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not part of the ideology; adherents split, with some fearing outside influence and others dismissing plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the conservative stress on markets, property and self-reliance in Kirk and Scruton; adherents split on public funding, so a mild lean.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Many conservatives favor markets but others prefer regulation, and Kirk stresses prudence over new taxes; cultural conservatism has no stated position.

future-generations.rationale: Burke's partnership between generations, the dead, living and unborn, and Kirk's stewardship principle support a duty to hand on a legacy.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from traditional views on sex roles often held by cultural conservatives, and its general skepticism of identity-based weighting.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed; conservatives are split between peace-through-strength hawks and others, and the ideology is about identity.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from Burke's and Kirk's trust in prudence and established elites over publicity in statecraft.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed; SEP notes conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine, so adherents split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Conservatives generally favour the state's monopoly of force; inferred from the order-preserving tradition in the SEP summary.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: loyalty to nation and duty to defend its heritage make refusal to fight unlikely.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: cultural conservatives tend toward market and individual arrangements, though adherents differ on economics.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between family-support and anti-welfare views.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: prudence and inherited burdens to future generations suggest favouring restraint on borrowing.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: the strand prioritises the home nation's culture over restructuring global rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Burke argues that institutions should be reformed gradually and not demolished, which rules out smashing the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Burke and Kirk defend inherited custom and prescription over untried blueprints, which cuts against open experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; conservatives are split between stewardship of nature and scepticism of pricing it.

sacred-nation.rationale: Burke's partnership between the dead, the living and the unborn describes the nation as an enduring community of meaning.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from fiscal restraint and scepticism of broad transfers; not stated.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: the strand stresses shared national heritage over frameworks of regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Kirk's principles and Burke affirm a permanent moral order and natural rights, so human nature is not to be redesigned.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between valuing public broadcasters as cultural institutions and opposing state-funded media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Cultural conservatives defend a particular inherited faith and heritage rather than treating all religions as one truth, so a mild disagree is inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Cultural conservatism is about heritage, not farm economics; SEP notes conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Consistent with this audit's lean towards an independent deterrent and the conservative priority on national security; inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: Conservatives favour broad parties and social harmony over class parties, as the audit's answers on workers' councils and class politics reflect; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred: the assimilationist, heritage-protecting strand holds that national law overrides customs that conflict with its own values.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the Burkean respect for inherited law and property, which in modern societies includes equal rights; the sources do not address this directly.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Cultural conservatives disagree among themselves, as Quebec-style language protection stresses a distinct language while Leitkultur arguments stress one national language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Conservatives respect common-law property protection but also accept regulation; the sources do not take a side, so it is left neutral.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Burke defends established institutions, but modern cultural conservatism works through elected legislatures; a formal chiefs' role is inferred as unlikely.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Conservatives value both stewardship of the land and liberty; the sources do not settle the priority, so it is left neutral.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Conservatives favour firm punishment but also defend judicial tradition and discretion, so adherents are split; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Wikipedia describes the family as assimilationist, and Leitkultur arguments make language a central duty of settling; this matches the audit's strong assimilation answer.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Cultural conservatism is about heritage, not labor law; SEP notes conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine, so adherents split.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on protecting national community and its institutions; restrictionist adherents typically back proof of citizenship at the ballot, though the sources do not discuss it.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the defense of the dominant culture's religious heritage, which adherents often want reflected in public life rather than neutral equal footing; not stated in the sources.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: SEP shows conservatives value inherited institutions and limits on popular will, but adherents differ on whether democracy is merely procedural; inferred, no stated position.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from Kirk's emphasis on custom, moral order and tradition, which adherents apply to marriage and sexual norms.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The ideology does not address internet shutdowns; order-minded adherents may accept them while liberty-minded ones object.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is outside the ideology's concern and adherents split between market and paternalist positions.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred: modern cultural conservatives accept women's equal political rights as settled national custom; the sources do not discuss it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from Kirk and Burke's view of religion as the foundation of moral order and culture, which adherents defend against such critiques.

race-social-construct.rationale: Adherents are split: many accept race as a social category while defending culture, others hold biological views; the sources do not address it.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the preference for custom and limited state, with adherents wary of dedicated equality bureaucracies; not stated in the sources.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: adherents split on property and markets, and SEP notes conservatives are not tied to one economic doctrine.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the attachment to national heritage and sovereignty, which makes supranational courts unwelcome to most adherents.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Adherents are split: religious conservatives read scripture literally while secular cultural conservatives defend religion as heritage only.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: cultural conservatives favour respecting group traditions and are wary of imposing requirements from outside.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: Burke and Kirk stress inherited institutions and property, so a planned state is unlikely to be defended.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: Burkean conservatives value tradition in institutions, but adherents differ on the mode of selection.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the defence of national heritage and traditional religion, which often includes recognising the traditional national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Wikipedia describes proponents as assimilationist, criticising parallel societies and ethnic enclaves, which counts against ethnic autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address disputed territory and adherents differ.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address colonial borders; Burkean caution about change suggests keeping them but it is not documented.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address simple living and adherents differ.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: cultural conservatives favour assimilation and free settlement within the nation rather than ethnic-homeland rules.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: adherents are split between traditional male-only duty and equal treatment.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Burke's partnership between the dead, the living and the unborn makes inherited land and culture a trust to be guarded for descendants.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from the conservative commitment to law, order and prescriptive legal tradition; the ideology does not address drug policy directly.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: cultural conservatism is about heritage rather than foreign economic alignment, and adherents split on China versus the United States.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from its concern for a nation's wider cultural community and heritage; the sources do not discuss kin minorities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Kirk ties property to freedom and order, so common ownership with compensation owed to all runs against the conservative view of property.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: SEP describes conservatism's organic, duty-laden view of society as opposed to atomistic individual rights.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: the ideology is not an economic program and adherents differ on taxation.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: cultural conservatism takes no fixed position on welfare design and adherents split between universal and targeted schemes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Burke and Kirk defend intermediate associations and inherited institutions between citizen and ruler rather than bypassing them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: favoritism toward businesses is an economic question on which cultural conservatives are not united.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the conservative view of religion as part of national heritage and public life, which favors religious identity in politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Kirk's principle of prudent, continuous change implies adopting modern means while preserving inherited custom, as the statement says.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from its defense of traditional family norms; the sources do not discuss divorce law and adherents vary.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from its protection of national heritage and sovereignty; resource ownership is not addressed in the sources.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Conservatism in the SEP is tied to property and prescription rather than pattern-based equality, so a weak lean to agree is inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Conservatives are generally wary of new taxes and economic engineering, and SEP notes no single economic doctrine; a weak lean to disagree is inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Cultural conservatives tend to stress culture and family over racism as causes of disadvantage; inferred, and adherents vary.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Burke-style conservatism (s3) values settled law and gradual reform over private judgement of justice; inferred lean to disagree.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Work and tradition are valued by conservatives, so a lean against mass automation to work far less is inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Cultural conservatives defend their own culture but split on the world order; inferred, so neutral.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Conservative thought rejects Marxist economics; a lean to disagree is inferred from its general principles.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Burke's attachment to country and its inherited institutions (s3) fits patriotism; the worker-solidarity link is inferred, so a weak lean to agree.

material-over-identity.rationale: Cultural conservatives emphasise culture themselves but are not a left movement; inferred, so neutral.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Conservatism is hostile to communist parties and their projects; inferred lean to disagree.

notes: Wikipedia distinguishes cultural from social conservatism (abortion, same-sex marriage) and from nationalism, so moral-issue answers are mostly medium confidence and economic answers mostly neutral and low. Many answers are inferences, so inclusion may be thin.
